title: Canonical MCP server model and transport types
description: Define in at-model the one MCP server representation every other layer converts to and from. McpServer { id: McpServerId, display_name, description: Option<String>, transport: McpTransport, scope: Scope, extra: BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value> for unknown native keys carried opaquely }. enum McpTransport { Stdio { command: String, args: Vec<String>, cwd: Option<PathBuf>, env: BTreeMap<String, EnvValue> }, Http { url: Url, headers: BTreeMap<String, EnvValue>, oauth: Option<OAuthProfile { issuer, client_id, scopes, token_ref } } }, and enum EnvValue { Literal(String), Secret(SecretRef { env_name, keychain_account }) }. Transport is an enum so stdio-only code cannot run on an http server. Conversions (canonical <-> per-agent projections) stay in at-adapters; this story only fixes the shape and its invariants.
acceptance: serde_json and serde_yaml-free round trip is stable: committed golden JSON of one stdio and one http server re-serialises byte-identically.
EnvValue::Secret stores only env_name plus keychain_account; a lint test asserts no struct field in at-model is named secret_value/token/secret with type String.
Unknown per-server keys captured in extra survive load then save of the canonical store unchanged and in original order.
Table-driven unit tests cover both transports, empty args, args with spaces/unicode/newlines, empty env, and cwd None vs Some.
notes: McpServerId is a newtype distinct from ItemId to prevent cross-use; at-store provides the ItemId bridge. OAuthProfile.token_ref is a Keychain account name, never a token.

title: MCP server validation rules
description: Validation module in at-model (pure functions, no IO beyond an injected PATH resolver trait) returning Vec<FieldError { field, code, message }> so the form renders inline errors. Name: ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,62}$ and must not end in a dot; duplicate id inside the same scope is DuplicateId, the same id in different scopes is allowed and yields a ShadowNotice. URL: must parse, scheme http or https, non-empty host, no userinfo (credentials in a URL are rejected with the message to use a header secret), no fragment. Stdio: command non-empty and free of NUL; existence is validated through the PATH resolver (TM-014) and reported as UnresolvedCommand warning, not a hard error, so a server can be saved before its binary is installed. Args: no NUL. Env names: ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$, duplicates rejected. Secret refs: keychain account non-empty, no control characters.
acceptance: 24-case table test covers valid and invalid names, URLs, env names and commands, asserting exact error codes.
Duplicate id in the same scope returns DuplicateId; the same id in User and Project returns Ok plus ShadowNotice naming the winning scope.
https://user:pass@host/mcp is rejected with code CredentialsInUrl and the form-ready message.
Saving a server whose command is missing from PATH succeeds with a warning; testing its connection fails with UnresolvedCommand (see TM-017).
Environment entries reject control characters and zero-width characters, verified by test cases.
notes: Name regex is deliberately lower-case because Codex tables and omp JSON keys are case-sensitive and the UI shows one name across three files.

title: Canonical AgenTuna MCP store document
description: at-store owns .agentuna/mcp.json (project), the User store copy and the Local copy. The file is content only: { schema_version: 1, servers: { <slug>: <McpServerDef> } }, sorted by slug, 2-space indent, trailing newline. Item identity, kind, scope and path live in store.json owned by TC-002, never here; the key is the slug and the ItemId comes from the manifest of the containing store (decision 3). Unknown top-level keys are preserved on rewrite. Writes go through the at-fs pipeline (TF-004): diff, backup, atomic rename, hash recheck. Reads tolerate a missing file (empty content) and reject schema_version > 1 with UnsupportedStoreVersion without touching the file. mcp.json holds MCP server definitions only; identity, kind, scope and path are owned by store.json (TC-002). Secrets appear only as EnvValue::Secret references.
acceptance: Load of a missing mcp.json returns empty content and does not create a file; a save writes only schema_version and servers, with no item id, kind, scope or path keys (schema-shape assertion).
A store with schema_version 2 returns UnsupportedStoreVersion and the file mtime/hash is unchanged afterwards.
Malformed JSON reports line and column, writes nothing, and leaves no .tmp file behind.
Saving after an external edit of an unrelated top-level key keeps that key verbatim.
Every save produces a backup entry via the at-fs pipeline (asserted with the temp-HOME fixture).
notes: mcp.json holds MCP server definitions only; item identity, kind, scope and path live in store.json owned by TC-002. Agent files are rendered artifacts.

title: MCP deployment intents and planner
description: Extend the at-engine planner for MCP: McpIntent::{Add, Edit, Rename, SetEnabledForAgent { agent, enabled }, DisableInRepo { project }, Promote, MoveToScope, Delete}. Each intent expands into a ChangeSet of FileOps by asking at-adapters for a projection per selected agent and scope. Enabling for an agent writes the server into that agent's target file; disabling uses the agent native flag where the capability matrix says it exists (omp enabled:false, Codex enabled=false), otherwise removes the entry and records a tombstone deployment row so re-enabling restores the exact prior entry. Locked Global entries return Locked with zero FileOps. Not-installed agents are rejected with AgentNotInstalled. DisableInRepo appends the item id to the `disabled` tombstone array in store.json owned by TC-002 and removes the key from repo-level renders only. Delete removes the server from every rendered file and marks the item deleted, never touching unmanaged native entries.
acceptance: Add on the three detected agents fixture yields exactly three FileOps with paths ~/.claude.json, ~/.codex/config.toml and ~/.omp/agent/mcp.json.
SetEnabledForAgent(false) writes enabled = false for Codex and enabled:false for omp, and removes the key for Claude while the tombstone restores a byte-identical entry on re-enable.
A locked server returns Locked and the planner returns an empty FileOps list (test asserts no IO is attempted).
DisableInRepo on Codex returns NotSupported with reason text and writes only the `disabled` tombstone array in store.json plus a warning row.
Rename to an existing id in the same scope fails with DuplicateId before any FileOp is produced.
notes: Why-trace rendering is owned by the engine slice; this story only produces the change plan and the `disabled` tombstone entry in store.json.

title: Claude Code MCP adapter (JSON, span patching)
description: Parse and render the Claude MCP surface: mcpServers at the root of ~/.claude.json, project entries at .projects["<abs path>"].mcpServers, and the repo-level .mcp.json. Use jsonc-parser CST and patch only the mcpServers member; never re-serialise the whole document, because Claude rewrites ~/.claude.json behind AgenTuna and the file carries unrelated multi-megabyte state. Map type stdio (default when absent), http and sse with url plus headers. Env values of the form ${NAME} become EnvValue::Secret when a matching ref exists, otherwise stay Literal and are preserved verbatim. Unknown per-server keys are retained. Preserve the file's existing indent, key order and trailing newline. When the config path is a symlink, set WriteRequest.follow_symlink=true (decision 5) so TF-004/TF-053 write through to the resolved target and keep the link; every other caller leaves the flag false. Before rename, recheck hash and mtime (TF-004); on ExternalWriteConflict re-read and re-apply once if the mcpServers subtree is unchanged, otherwise return the conflict to the caller.
acceptance: Golden fixture load then save with no edits is byte-identical, including formatting of unrelated top-level keys; with a symlinked fixture path, WriteRequest.follow_symlink is true, the target gains the change and the path remains a symlink.
Adding one server produces a diff of plus-lines only inside mcpServers and leaves every other byte identical.
A project-scope write targets .projects["<path>"].mcpServers and does not create a sibling project object or drop existing fields.
A server named with a dot, hyphen or unicode character round-trips through the JSON key unchanged.
Simulated external rewrite between read and rename returns ExternalWriteConflict and leaves the file at the external writer's version; a second attempt with an unchanged subtree succeeds.
notes: Verified on this Mac: user-level servers live in ~/.claude.json root mcpServers with type/command/args/env; a project server appears under .projects.<path>.mcpServers.

title: Codex MCP adapter (TOML, format preserving)
description: Read and write [mcp_servers.<name>] tables in ~/.codex/config.toml with toml_edit so comments, blank lines, key order and unrelated tables (projects, features, plugins, marketplaces) survive untouched. Map command, args, env (string table), env_vars (array of names), cwd, enabled, startup_timeout_sec and url. Quote table keys that contain a dot or quote so [mcp_servers."a.b"] does not create a nested table. New tables are appended after the last existing mcp_servers table to keep the group together; deletion removes the table and its trailing blank line without touching the next table header. Env values stay literal strings in the file, never values. A ${NAME} env value is written as text and flagged UnverifiedInterpolation (see TM-008) instead of being silently converted.
acceptance: Golden config fixture with comments, blank lines and unrelated tables round-trips byte-identical when no edit is requested.
Adding mcp_servers.github inserts a comment-free table after the final mcp_servers table and the diff touches no other line.
A server id containing a dot renders as [mcp_servers."a.b"] and parses back to id a.b; a quote in the id is escaped and round-trips.
Deleting a server removes exactly its table and its trailing blank line, leaving the next header intact.
env_vars and enabled values written in an existing file are preserved when only command changes.
notes: Verified shapes on this Mac: [mcp_servers.playwright] command+args, [mcp_servers.node_repl] with env_vars and startup_timeout_sec, [mcp_servers.shuttle] url only, [mcp_servers.computer-use] with cwd and enabled. Whether Codex expands ${VAR} inside env values is UNVERIFIED.

title: omp MCP adapter (mcp.json)
description: Read and write ~/.omp/agent/mcp.json. Preserve the top-level $schema key and any unknown top-level or per-server keys. Per-server shape: type stdio or http, command, args, env object, enabled boolean, url for http; a missing type is inferred as stdio. Create the file when absent with the $schema value copied from an existing file if present, otherwise {"$schema": "https://.../mcp.schema.json", "mcpServers": {}} and 0644 permissions. Same span-patch and concurrency rules as the other JSON adapter (TF-004). Also check ~/.omp/agent/skills sibling conventions only to resolve the agent home, not the MCP file.
acceptance: Golden mcp.json fixture round-trips byte-identical with no edits, $schema included.
Adding an http server writes type, url and enabled at the top level of its entry and no command key.
A file with an unknown top-level key such as $schema plus a custom key keeps both after a write.
Missing file is created once with $schema and an empty mcpServers object; a second save does not duplicate the header.
An entry with enabled:false keeps enabled:false through an unrelated edit to args.
notes: Verified on this Mac: mcpServers entries use type stdio|http, enabled booleans, and an http entry is url-only (shuttle). Whether omp expands ${VAR} in mcp.json env values is UNVERIFIED.

title: Agent MCP capability matrix and unsupported-field policy
description: Registry capability(agent) -> AgentMcpCapabilities { supports_http, supports_headers, supports_env, env_interpolation: Verified | Unverified | Unsupported, supports_enabled_flag, supports_project_scope, name_rules, config_paths }. Immediate truth table: Claude http yes, headers yes, env yes, interpolation Verified for .mcp.json and Unverified for ~/.claude.json, enabled flag no, project scope yes; Codex http via url yes, headers Unverified/not modelled, env yes, env_vars pass-through yes, interpolation Unverified, enabled flag yes, project scope no; omp http yes, headers Unverified, env yes, interpolation Unverified, enabled flag yes, project scope yes. Projection returns RenderedEntry plus Vec<UnsupportedField>; policy is explicit drop-with-warning recorded on the deployment row and shown in the save dialog, never silent loss and never a bogus key. Cursor and custom agents are served by GenericMcpWriter { format: Json | Toml, file_path, key_path: Vec<String> such as ["mcpServers"] for JSON or ["mcp_servers"] for TOML, field_map: agent field names to canonical fields, name_quoting: Bare | AlwaysQuoted }, which reuses the same span-patching JSON and toml_edit machinery parameterised by key path instead of new adapter code. That covers a custom agent whose file is settings.json with a mcpServers object, a TOML config with [mcp_servers.<name>] tables, and Cursor's ~/.cursor/mcp.json, which is registered as installed=false on this machine and uses this generic path.
acceptance: Snapshot test pins the capability matrix for claude_code, codex, omp, cursor and a custom agent, including not_installed flags read by both the form and the planner.
Projecting an http server with headers to Codex returns the entry plus UnsupportedField(headers) and the rendered TOML contains no headers key.
Saving with at least one unsupported field requires the UI acknowledgement flag or returns UnsupportedFieldsUnacknowledged (asserted by test).
A config path that is a symlink into a dotfiles repo is written through and the link is still a symlink afterwards.

GenericMcpWriter round-trips a Cursor-shaped JSON file (mcpServers at root, stdio and url entries) and a custom TOML file (mcp_servers tables) with key-path parameterisation, preserving unknown sibling keys and creating the key path when absent.
notes: Any Unverified cell must be resolved by the probe stories (TM-013, TM-029) and the matrix updated with evidence; UNVERIFIED today: Codex and omp ${VAR} expansion, Claude headers on ~/.claude.json, omp headers.

title: health_checks queries, status mapping and retention
description: Repository and retention layer over the TF-015 health_checks table; this story owns no DDL (decision 8). Row semantics use the TF-015 column names exactly: item_id (server identity), server_name for display, scope, project_id, transport, checked_at (unix ms), status in ok|failed|unknown|skipped_offline, trigger in manual|scheduled|startup, latency_ms, tools_count, error_code, error_text_redacted. Queries: last_n(item_id, 5), status_of(item_id), failing_servers(scope), history(item_id, from, to), each mapping status to the UI dot. TM-009 is the single owner of health_checks retention: delete all but the newest 200 rows per item_id, pruned hourly by one background task. Aggregated last status is a query, not a duplicated column. unknown means a check never completed; skipped_offline means an HTTP check suppressed by network policy (TF-036).
acceptance: Module issues no DDL: a test asserts its SQL strings contain no CREATE, ALTER or DROP and that every query runs against a schema-v1 database.
last_n returns the five newest rows in descending checked_at order and tolerates fewer than five; status values round-trip as ok, failed, unknown and skipped_offline.
Retention test inserts 250 rows for one server, runs the hourly prune, and asserts exactly the newest 200 remain with the 50 oldest gone.
failing_servers returns only servers whose newest row has status=failed and excludes servers never checked or last seen as unknown.
An error_text_redacted longer than 512 chars is truncated by the writer and never contains a resolved secret (asserted with a sentinel).
notes: health_checks DDL and its status CHECK constraint live in TF-015; this story owns only queries and the hourly pruning job, so retention has exactly one owner in the plan.

title: secret_refs and secret_ref_uses inventory queries
description: Inventory and repository layer over TF-018 secret_refs plus secret_ref_uses; this story owns no DDL (decision 8). Reads ref metadata (name, keychain_service, created_at, rotated_at, last_read_ok_at) and usage rows (secret_name, item_id, scope). Queries: inventory() with use_count and last_read_ok_at, referenced_by(name) returning item_id, scope and slug via the items table, orphaned() listing refs with no usage row, and missing_keychain() comparing refs against at-secrets existence. Delete is a repository call that reports referencing items and requires confirm=true. No column and no query result carries a value; the engine refuses to render a server whose reference has no Keychain item.
acceptance: Module issues no DDL: a test asserts its SQL strings contain no CREATE, ALTER or DROP and that every query runs against the TF-018 schema.
inventory returns one row per ref with use_count equal to its secret_ref_uses rows and passes last_read_ok_at through unchanged.
referenced_by returns every item_id plus scope for a name, including two uses of the same name in different scopes, and zero rows when the name is unused.
orphaned returns refs with no usage row; delete without confirm=true returns ReferencedSecret with the count and changes nothing.
A missing Keychain item for an existing ref makes projection fail with MissingSecret instead of writing an empty env value.
notes: secret_refs and secret_ref_uses DDL live in TF-018. Keychain remains the source of truth for existence, checked on read.

title: Keychain create/read/rotate/delete via at-secrets
description: at-secrets wraps keyring 4.x with service dev.agentuna.mcp and account = keychain_account. API: create(name, value) fails if present unless rotate, read(name) -> SecretString (zeroize on drop), rotate(name, value), delete(name), exists(name). Values are never formatted, never in Debug/Display, never in error payloads, and never passed as a process argument. Map platform errors: keychain locked, user denied, interaction not allowed (GUI prompt suppressed for background checks), not found. On delete, also remove the secret_refs row in the same logical operation and report referencing servers first. Concurrent reads must be safe from the scheduler thread and the UI thread.
acceptance: Round trip create/read/rotate/delete passes against the keychain stub used by TF-010, and against the real Keychain in a manual smoke test.
create on an existing name returns AlreadyExists and leaves the stored value unchanged; rotate overwrites and returns Ok.
delete of a missing name returns NotFound without panicking or prompting.
A denied or locked keychain maps to KeychainDenied with instruction text naming Keychain Access and the service name; no value appears in the error.
Two threads reading the same secret concurrently both receive the correct value (loom-free stress test, 100 iterations).
notes: keyring 4.x does not enumerate items, so listing is served by secret_refs (TM-010); a listing mismatch is reported as drift in the inventory.

title: ${VAR} reference syntax, resolution and redaction
description: Parse and validate ${NAME} references in env values and http headers. Grammar accepted in AgenTuna: ${NAME} exactly, where NAME matches ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$. On import, ${NAME:-default} is accepted and converted to a Literal plus a warning, because a default that is not a secret must not masquerade as one. Resolution happens only at the moment a process is spawned or a header is built, never at save. Unresolved reference returns MissingSecret { name } and blocks the operation. A Redactor holds the set of resolved values for the current session and masks them as *** in stderr capture, error chains, toasts, log lines, and the panic hook, matching by longest value first to avoid partial exposure.
acceptance: Parser table covers ${A}, ${A_B1}, ${}, ${A B}, $A, $${A}, ${A:-x} and nested braces with exact outcomes.
resolve of ${MISSING} returns MissingSecret naming MISSING and no partial substitution is written anywhere.
Redactor replaces a 40-character sentinel appearing three times in a 64 KiB stderr buffer with *** and leaves the rest byte-identical.
Debug formatting of every at-secrets type and of EnvValue::Secret never prints a resolved value (asserted by a formatting test).
A ${NAME:-default} import produces a Literal of the default plus a warning, and the resulting file contains no ${} wrapper.
notes: Redaction is defence in depth; the primary guarantee is that values are never put on disk or in argv in the first place.

title: Per-agent launch-time secret injection strategy
description: Decide and implement how each agent sees a secret at launch, driven by the capability matrix. Claude Code expands ${VAR} from the environment of the claude process for .mcp.json (documented); writing the ref is correct when the variable is exported in the launching shell. Codex: write env_vars = ["NAME"] so Codex passes the variable through from its own environment (shape verified in the local config), and never write env value = ${NAME} as a promise the binary does not keep. omp: UNVERIFIED whether mcp.json expands ${VAR}; until a probe proves it, AgenTuna writes no secret ref into omp's env and shows a warning row on the deployment. For every agent with interpolation Unsupported or Unverified, the form offers Copy shell snippet that reads the value from Keychain at shell start (security find-generic-password -s dev.agentuna.mcp -a NAME -w) and exports it; the snippet contains the account name only. No path in this story writes a value to a file.
acceptance: Table-driven test: for each of claude_code, codex and omp, saving a server with a secret produces the documented shape and never the sentinel value (file scan assertion).
Codex output contains env_vars with the variable name and no env entry for that name.
omp and other Unverified agents produce a deployment warning listing the variable name and the snippet, and the saved file contains no ${} reference for that variable.
Copy shell snippet text contains the keychain service and account and no secret value (test compares against the generated text).
The docs table in notes is updated with probe results and dated; any UNVERIFIED cell is labelled UNVERIFIED until measured.
notes: UNVERIFIED today: whether Codex expands ${VAR} in env values; whether omp expands ${VAR} in mcp.json; whether ~/.claude.json env values expand for user-scope servers. Probe with a fixture server that echoes its env in stderr.

title: PATH and command resolution for GUI-launched agents
description: A Finder-launched app inherits a minimal PATH that lacks Homebrew and version-manager shims, so npx/uvx resolution fails while the same command works in the user's terminal. Implement PATH discovery: run $SHELL -l -c 'printf %s "$PATH"' with a 2 s timeout, cache for 60 s, merge with /opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin. Provide which(command) returning the absolute path plus a source tag, detect npx/node under nvm, asdf, mise, Volta and fnm layouts when not on PATH and return a specific hint, and use the resolved absolute path for spawns so behaviour matches the check. On timeout or shell failure, fall back to the default list and mark the result degraded. Windows path rules are out of scope for this story but the trait has a stub.
acceptance: With a fixture PATH containing /opt/homebrew/bin/npx, which returns that absolute path and source login_shell.
With a shell that hangs, resolution returns the default-list result after 2 s and sets degraded=true.
A fake ~/.nvm/versions/node/v20/bin/npx not on PATH produces a hint naming nvm and the version directory.
A command that exists but is not executable returns NotExecutable, distinct from NotFound.
Repeated calls within 60 s do not re-run the login shell (call counter asserted).
notes: Spawn uses the resolved absolute path; the stored command string stays as the user typed it for portability across machines.

title: stdio session harness: spawn, handshake, tools, shutdown escalation
description: at-mcp stdio client on rmcp and tokio: spawn the resolved command in its own process group with cwd when set, env = inherited parent env plus resolved server env values, no secret in argv. Timeouts: startup 180 s when the command basename is npx, pnpm, bunx, uvx or pipx (first run downloads), 20 s otherwise; initialize 20 s; tools/list 15 s per page with cursor pagination capped at 500 tools. Drain stderr continuously into an 8 KiB ring buffer so a chatty server cannot block on a full pipe. Shutdown: SIGINT, wait 2 s, SIGTERM, wait 3 s, SIGKILL, always signalling the whole process group (killpg on Unix, taskkill /T /F on Windows) so npx's node child dies too; reap zombies; cancel token honoured at every await.
acceptance: Fixture server that ignores SIGINT exits on SIGTERM within 3 s and the test records the signal sequence SIGINT then SIGTERM.
Fixture server that ignores both is SIGKILLed and the test asserts no surviving child in its process group.
A server writing 1 MiB to stderr before the handshake still completes initialize and tools/list.
A server that sleeps 30 s before initialize with a non-npx command fails at 20 s with kind StartupTimeout and the UI-ready message.
npx-kind command gets the 180 s budget (asserted from the timeout policy table, not by sleeping).
notes: rmcp provides the child process transport; AgenTuna owns the timeout policy, stderr capture and process-group kill.

title: HTTP/streamable transport and OAuth sign-in
description: HTTP client for streamable HTTP servers using rmcp's HTTP transport plus its auth support. Sign-in: fetch protected resource metadata (RFC 9728) and authorization server metadata (RFC 8414), register a client dynamically when no client id is stored (RFC 7591), start PKCE S256 with state, open the system browser to the authorization URL, receive the code on a loopback listener at http://127.0.0.1:<ephemeral>/callback with a 120 s wait and Cancel, verify state and code_verifier, exchange for tokens, store access and refresh tokens in Keychain under oauth:<server-id>:<issuer> (never in mcp.json), and refresh with a 60 s expiry skew. A 401 on tools/list triggers one refresh and one retry, then surfaces SignInRequired. If the browser cannot be opened, the URL is copied to the clipboard and shown. TLS errors are reported as TlsError, never retried.
acceptance: Fake authorization server fixture completes the loopback flow and the token lands in the keychain stub, not in any file under the temp HOME.
A wrong state parameter or a mismatched code_verifier is rejected with OAuthStateMismatch and the callback returns an error page.
An expired access token is refreshed once transparently; two consecutive 401s return SignInRequired and do not loop.
Cancelling sign-in closes the listener and leaves no partial token rows.
All OAuth network calls happen only after an explicit user action (test asserts zero requests before Sign in is invoked).
notes: Versions of rmcp auth features must be pinned at implementation time; if a piece is missing, the RFC steps above are implemented directly and noted.

title: Test-connection API and error taxonomy
description: Single entry point at-mcp::test_connection(server, scope) -> TestResult { ok, server_name, server_version, transport, latency_ms, tools_count, tools: Vec<ToolSummary { name, description }>, error: Option<McpError>, stderr_excerpt }. Steps: resolve secrets, spawn or connect, initialize with clientInfo AgenTuna/<version>, list tools with pagination, measure latency from spawn to the first tools/list response, shut down cleanly. Error kinds: UnresolvedCommand, NotExecutable, PermissionDenied, StartupTimeout, HandshakeTimeout, ToolListTimeout, ProtocolVersionMismatch, Unauthorized401, SignInRequired, TlsError, ServerError { code, message }, TransportUnsupported, Cancelled. Every error carries a redacted message and a suggested action string used by the Fix token and Sign in buttons. Results are returned over the app bridge and never cached as health until the scheduler writes them.
acceptance: Successful run against the stdio fixture returns ok, tools_count 26 on the fixture, latency_ms greater than 0 and the sorted tool names.
Each error kind is produced by a dedicated fixture or injected failure in the table test (at least 10 kinds).
The API returns within 1 s when cancelled, and shutdown still completes without leaking a child process.
stderr_excerpt is truncated to 2 KiB and passes through the Redactor; a sentinel secret in stderr appears as ***.
Test connection never writes a health_checks row and never mutates an agent file (asserted by file hashes before and after).
notes: The UI shows tool names as chips plus +N more (see TM-023); the API returns the full list so the detail screen can expand it.

title: Health scheduler with backoff and visibility pause
description: Background scheduler driven by TF-023 settings: health_interval_minutes (0 = off, 5, 15 or 60, default 5) sets the cadence with up to 30 s jitter, and background_health (off|local|all, default local) sets the scope. local schedules checks only for stdio servers that already have at least one manual test; HTTP servers are scheduled only when background_health=all, and every scheduled HTTP check executes as the registered TF-036 NetworkAction so the network policy gate applies. One check per server in flight (a slow check skips its next tick and is marked running long rather than stacking). Failure backoff per server 5, 10, 20, 40, 60 minutes capped, reset to the base cadence on success. Pause when the app window is hidden, minimised or the app is inactive for more than 60 s; on becoming visible again, run overdue checks staggered over 0 to 2 s. Cancel everything on quit within 5 s via CancellationToken and the same shutdown escalation as TM-015. Persist every result through TM-009 with trigger=scheduled, publish status changes over the bridge as Tauri events, and coalesce identical consecutive failures so the UI does not stream noise. Offline detection: when the network is down, HTTP servers are recorded as skipped_offline without counting as failures.
acceptance: With health_interval_minutes=0 no scheduled checks run; with 5, 15 and 60 the fake clock shows exactly those gaps within the 30 s jitter bound.

background_health=local schedules stdio servers only after their first manual test and never schedules HTTP servers; all schedules HTTP servers with each run recorded as a TF-036 NetworkAction; off schedules nothing.

A failing server is retried at 5, 10, 20, 40 and 60 minute gaps and a passing check resets the gap to the base interval; hiding the window pauses checks and showing it runs overdue checks within the 0 to 2 s stagger.
A server whose check takes longer than the interval produces no overlapping calls (in-flight counter never exceeds 1); quit during an in-flight check returns within 5 s and leaves no child process.
A simulated offline network writes skipped_offline rows for http servers and no rows for stdio servers.
notes: Settings keys come from TF-023 (health_interval_minutes, background_health); the NetworkAction registry is TF-036 and scheduled HTTP checks never bypass it. Visibility is read from Tauri window focus/visibility events.

title: Failing-state surfacing to Overview and list
description: Turn health rows into UI-facing state: per server LatestHealth { dot: Healthy | Failing | Disabled | NotTested | RunningCheck, latency_ms, short_reason }, a scope-level summary for the Overview Needs attention list, and a transition detector that fires exactly one notification per healthy-to-failing transition and re-arms only after a success. Failing entries carry the suggested action from TM-017 so the Fix token, Sign in or Review config button can be rendered inline. Disabled-in-repo servers show as Disabled in the repo scope instead of Failing. Summaries are computed by one query per scope, not per row.
acceptance: Server whose newest health row has status=ok shows Healthy and the latency in ms; with newest status=failed shows Failing plus the short reason such as 401 Unauthorized.
healthy-to-failing fires one event; three further failing checks fire none; a success re-arms the detector.
Overview summary for the User scope counts exactly the failing servers and links each to its detail route.
A server disabled in the current repo renders Disabled in that repo scope and is excluded from the failing count.
Zero servers or zero checks produces NotTested and an empty needs-attention list, not an error.
notes: Overview screen rendering itself belongs to the shell slice (F03); this story supplies the data and the single-fire transition event.

title: MCP Servers list screen
description: ui/src/screens/mcp_list. Header with count line (N servers, X managed by AgenTuna, Y live only in agent config files) and Add server button. Native banner hosted from TC-025 when native-only servers exist; the screen renders the banner's Review & migrate action and owns no banner dismissal state. Filter chips All, Global, User, Project, Not in AgenTuna, Failing with live counts, plus a filter box matching name, command and URL. Table via the TU-003 component: name plus transport/command subtitle, scope badge with lock glyph for Global locked, one cell per detected agent, health column, truncation menu. Row states: linked toggle on, linked off, native with path and either Adopt or Resolve, none, locked with tooltip, shadowed. States: loading skeleton, empty (no servers, with Add and Review & migrate), error (store unreadable, with Retry), populated. Row open navigates to detail; row menu opens TM-025.
acceptance: Renders all six chip counts from the same query the table uses, so counts always equal visible rows per chip.
Empty state appears on a fresh store and its Add server button routes to TM-022.
Native-only row shows the absolute source path and both Adopt and Resolve actions, and Adopt is disabled when the item is already adopted.
Locked Global row shows a lock glyph, the toggle is non-interactive, and a tooltip states the scope that locks it.
Store-read error renders an error state with Retry, and Retry re-runs the query without restarting the app.
notes: Filtering and sorting are client-side on the loaded list; the virtualised table handles 500 rows without dropping frames.

title: MCP server detail screen
description: ui/src/screens/mcp_detail. Header: name, scope badge, description, actions Disable in this repo, Test connection, Edit. Left column Configuration (transport, defined in with the list of resolved file paths, command plus args, environment rows showing KEY and a Keychain chip with the account name), Tools (chips, +N more expands), state panel. Right column Health (status line, last 5 checks as coloured squares with tooltips, cadence text every 5 min, contextual button Fix token or Sign in), Loaded by (per-agent toggles, not-installed agents greyed with the reason), Why is this on (one-sentence trace and Open trace). States: loading, error (server missing after external delete, with Back), OAuth required, running test with spinner plus Cancel, test result with latency and tool count, disabled-in-repo variant.
acceptance: Loaded by toggles call SetEnabledForAgent and reflect the new state within one render after the engine reply, with a toast from TM-025 on failure.
Health strip renders exactly five slots, oldest last, coloured by ok, and shows Not tested when there are no rows.
A failing server with an auth error shows Fix token, an OAuth server with no token shows Sign in, and both open TM-026.
Command, args and env render with monospace cells; a secret row shows the Keychain account name and never a value.
Deleting the server file entry externally while the screen is open shows the missing-server error on the next refresh rather than a panic.
notes: Open trace routes to the engine why-trace view; this screen only renders the one-line summary.

title: Add MCP server form: fields, validation, scope and agents
description: ui/src/screens/mcp_form in Add mode. Fields: Name, Transport segmented stdio/HTTP, Command with a resolved-path hint or warning, Arguments (one per row, add and remove), Environment editor rows KEY plus a value slot that is either a Keychain reference chip or a literal, plus Add variable, helper text Files get ${NAME}; the value itself never lands on disk. Scope radio cards Global (Needs admin, disabled when not permitted), User (best for personal tokens), Project (committed), plus a collapsed Local (only you, this repo) option that expands on click and saves into .agentuna/local/ (decision 4); the selected state is persisted per session. Agents checkboxes: not-installed agents disabled with a not installed label, installed ones checked by default per the user setting. Inline per-field errors from TM-002 on blur and on submit; duplicate id across the open scopes shown at the name field with the scope that owns it. Transport HTTP swaps Command for URL plus headers editor and a Sign in panel placeholder. Save label reflects the scope (Save to User scope), Cancel returns to the list. States: pristine, dirty, validating, saving, save failed with a per-file reason.
acceptance: Submitting an empty form marks Name, Command/URL and at least one agent as errors and does not call the engine.
Switching transport stdio to HTTP and back preserves the previously typed command and args in the form state.
A duplicate name shows the owning scope immediately, and Save stays disabled until the name changes.

Cursors and the Global scope card appear disabled with an explanatory tooltip when the agent is absent or admin is unavailable, and the Local option stays collapsed until clicked, then routes the save to .agentuna/local/.
Saving writes the server, shows a success toast, clears the form and routes to detail, with all three selected agent files updated.
notes: Form state is one struct with a dirty flag; validation runs on the same pure functions the engine uses so the form cannot accept what the planner will reject.

title: Form side panels: test connection and files-that-will-change
description: Two reusable panels used by both add and edit. Test connection panel: idle state with Run test, running state with elapsed time and Cancel, success state with Connected, tool count, latency and tool chips plus +N more, failure state with the error kind, redacted message, stderr excerpt in a collapsible block and a suggested action (Fix token, Sign in, Check command). Result is per current form values, not the saved server, and is invalidated when any field changes. Files that will change panel: one row per selected agent and scope with the resolved path, agent name, plus and minus line counts, and a backup-first note; a collapsible diff via the TU-007 viewer showing the exact hunk for that file. Rows that cannot be written show the reason (permission denied, agent not installed, file changed on disk) and Save is disabled until that agent is deselected.
acceptance: Editing any field after a successful test clears the result and shows the stale badge until Run test is pressed again.
Diff preview for the Claude target contains the new server key and no other change, matching the engine's planned FileOp byte for byte.
A read-only target file renders a permission-denied row, keeps that agent selected but blocks Save, and Deselect this agent re-enables Save.
Test against an unreachable URL shows a redacted error plus Sign in when the error is SignInRequired.
Tool list shows the first 5 names then +N more, and expanding reveals all returned names.
notes: The diff panel renders the planner's preview from the same ChangeSet that Save will apply, so preview drift is impossible by construction.

title: Edit MCP server form with prefilled state and diff-before-save
description: ui/src/screens/mcp_form in Edit mode: prefilled from the canonical server with the target scope fixed to the item's own scope and a Move to another scope action that routes through the promote flow. Track a dirty flag; Save is disabled when clean. Before applying, show a confirmation summary when the edit is destructive: rename (lists agent files that lose the old key), transport change (lists keys that are removed), scope change (lists files that change) and unsupported-field drops from TM-008. The confirmation embeds the files-that-will-change panel and requires an explicit Apply. Cancel with unsaved changes prompts Discard changes. Concurrent external edit returns ExternalWriteConflict and shows Keep mine (re-apply) or Reload.
acceptance: Open then Save without edits produces zero FileOps (dirty tracking asserted).
Editing only the environment of an existing server yields a diff limited to that env entry in every selected agent file.
Renaming github to github-enterprise opens the confirmation listing all files that lose the old key and gains the new key, and Cancel leaves every file unchanged.
An unsupported field drop requires the acknowledgement checkbox before Apply is enabled.
An ExternalWriteConflict response renders the two-button dialog and neither button is applied without a click.
notes: Edit reuses the add form component with a mode tag; no duplicated field logic.

title: Server row menu, disable and delete confirmations, toasts
description: at-ui/src/overlays/menus and dialogs. Row and detail overflow menu items: Open, Edit, Why is this on?, Test connection, Disable in this repo, Delete server. Disable in this repo opens a confirm dialog naming the repo and the server and explaining what stops loading where; when the agent has no project-level MCP scope the dialog states that the server will stay available for that agent and offers Disable for this agent instead. Delete server opens a destructive confirm listing affected files and requiring the server name typed when it is referenced in three or more files; it never deletes a native unmanaged entry. Results use the TU-005 toast service: saved, test result, locked, shadowed, native adopt first, conflict. Escape closes each dialog without acting.
acceptance: Every menu item routes to the documented destination; Open on a native-only row routes to adopt instead of detail.
Confirming Disable in this repo appends to the `disabled` tombstone array in store.json (TC-002) and shows one success toast; cancelling performs no write (file hash unchanged).
Delete on a server referenced by three files requires the exact typed name and the confirm button stays disabled until it matches.
Attempting a toggle on a locked server shows the locked toast and leaves the toggle visually unchanged.
Escape and clicking the scrim both close the dialog with no side effect.
notes: Toast copy is shared with the skills slice so wording stays consistent across item kinds.

title: Secret picker, inventory screen and Fix token flow
description: Three surfaces, one component set. Secret picker overlay opened from an env row: search across known refs, shows name, account, used-by count and last read result, with Create new secret inline (name, value masked, confirm value, never echoed, cleared on close), Rotate and Delete. Fix token flow: from a failing server, a focused dialog to rotate the referenced secret with a live Test connection that must pass before Done; the value is held only in memory. Secret inventory screen under the account menu Keychain secrets: table of name, account, referencing servers, created, rotated, last read ok, with orphan cleanup and no value display anywhere, plus an empty state explaining that servers add secrets on save. All text fields are zeroized on drop and the clipboard paste path never logs.
acceptance: Picker lists exactly the refs whose name matches the search, and selecting one assigns ${NAME} to the env row without touching the value.
Create new secret writes to Keychain and to secret_refs, shows it as used by the current form, and the reveal control is absent (value is never rendered).
Fix token with a wrong token shows the test failure and keeps Done disabled; with a good token Done updates the server only if the test passed.
Inventory shows no value column, and orphaned refs can be removed only after a confirm naming the ref.
Closing the picker or the dialog clears in-memory buffers (test asserts the zeroizing wrapper was dropped).
notes: Account-menu placement is owned by the shell slice (O04); this story provides the screen body and the picker overlay.

title: agentuna mcp and secret commands with JSON output
description: Register the noun-first `mcp` group and the nested `mcp secret` group on the TU-026 command tree, then implement: agentuna mcp list [--scope] [--json], mcp show <id> --json, mcp test <id> [--json] (exit codes per TU-033: 0 success, 1 failure, 2 usage error), mcp enable|disable <id> --agent <agent> [--scope], mcp add|edit from a JSON file on stdin, mcp secret list --json, mcp secret set <name> reading the value from stdin only (refused when stdin is a TTY without --no-echo handled by the terminal, and always refused as an argv value), mcp secret rm <name> --force. Every command goes through the same engine and adapter code as the UI. JSON output uses the TU-033 envelope (schema version with data or error) and stable field names, and never a secret value, a token, or a resolved env value; errors are {code, message, action} inside that envelope with the redacted message. No colour when --no-color or not a TTY.
acceptance: mcp list --json emits one object per server with id, scope, transport, per-agent state and health, and matches the UI count for the fixture HOME.
mcp test --json returns the tool count, latency and tool names in the TU-033 success envelope, and exit code 1 with a TU-033 error envelope on failure.
mcp secret set with the value passed as an argument is rejected before any Keychain call, with a message pointing at stdin.
Output of every command is scanned by the test for a sentinel secret and contains zero occurrences.
mcp disable on a locked server exits 2 with a TU-033 error envelope carrying code Locked and performs no write.
notes: CLI is the agent-operable surface (X11); it must be usable non-interactively from a script with no prompts.

title: Golden-file round-trip suite for all three MCP formats
description: Test module with fixtures per agent: Claude with a multi-MB ~/.claude.json shape (root mcpServers, projects map, unrelated keys), Claude project .mcp.json, Codex config.toml with comments, dotted keys, arrays of tables and unrelated sections, omp mcp.json with $schema and enabled flags. For each fixture assert: load then save with no edit is byte-identical; a single-field edit changes only the intended span (compare unified diff against a committed expected diff); comments, blank lines, key order, indentation and line endings survive; CRLF input stays CRLF; unicode and emoji in args survive; duplicate JSON keys and invalid TOML are rejected without writes; a symlinked config file stays a symlink. Fixtures include a server named with a dot and a server with 40 args.
acceptance: At least 8 fixtures run in CI and every no-op round trip is byte-identical (hash compare, not string equality after trim).
Each edit case's unified diff equals the committed expected diff file, so an accidental whole-file re-serialisation fails loudly.
CRLF, tabs and unusual indentation fixtures keep their exact bytes after edit.
Malformed fixtures produce a parse error and the file hash is unchanged, with no stray temp file in the directory.
Symlink fixture: after a write the path is still a symlink and the target contains the change.
notes: Expected diffs are committed next to fixtures so reviews show intent, not just green ticks.

title: Secrets never written to disk or logs
description: Adversarial test suite that plants a unique sentinel value in the keychain stub, exercises create, add server, test connection (stdout, stderr, error path), rotate, Fix token, CSV-free export, backup, crash and restart, then scans: every file under the temp HOME, the AgenTuna store, SQLite database files and WAL, backup directories, diff previews, toast and log sinks, panic output, and the process argv of spawned children. Any occurrence fails the test with the path and offset. Also assert that error payloads serialised to JSON for the CLI contain no sentinel, and that a child process receives the secret only through its environment, never as an argument.
acceptance: Sentinel scan runs over at least 200 files plus the SQLite main and WAL files and reports zero hits.
A spawned fixture server's /proc or ps argv line contains no sentinel while its environment does (asserted on macOS by ps -E output restricted to the test pid).
A forced panic after a secret is loaded writes no sentinel to the panic log or the crash report buffer.
Backup files created during the flow contain ${NAME} references only.
The test fails on a deliberately leaked sentinel (self-test) so the scanner is proven to work.
notes: Self-test of the scanner is mandatory; a scanner that cannot fail proves nothing.

title: Scheduler tests with fake clock and flaky fixture server
description: Deterministic tests for TM-018 using tokio time pausing and a fixture MCP server whose behaviour switches between pass, fail, hang and partial responses via a control file. Cover base cadence, jitter bound, backoff ladder, reset on success, single-flight, visibility pause and resume, staggered catch-up, offline handling, retention interaction (rows written then pruned), and quit cancellation. Assert no more than one in-flight check per server at any simulated instant and that the UI bridge receives one coalesced event per state change.
acceptance: Backoff ladder test asserts the exact simulated minute gaps 5, 10, 20, 40, 60, 60 and a reset after pass.
Hang fixture (never responds) is cancelled at the per-check deadline and counted as a failure without blocking the next server.
Hidden window over 30 simulated minutes writes zero scheduled rows; visible again writes exactly one per due server within 2 simulated seconds.
Quit test asserts all tasks joined within 5 s and the fixture process tree is empty.
Bridge event count equals state transitions, not check count (10 failing checks produce 1 failing event).
notes: Time starts paused; no test sleeps for real, so the suite stays under a few seconds.

title: stdio lifecycle and error-taxonomy fixtures
description: Fixture binaries in the test workspace implement the MCP handshake with configurable misbehaviour: normal 26 tools, paginated tools (3 pages), 1 MiB stderr burst, ignore SIGINT, ignore SIGINT and SIGTERM, never initialise, wrong protocol version, exit code 1 mid-call, refuse to spawn (missing binary), not executable, and an npx-like slow starter sleeping 25 s. Tests assert the timeout policy, escalation sequence and timings, stderr ring buffer bounds, orphan absence, and that each misbehaviour maps to the exact McpError kind in TM-017.
acceptance: Every error kind in the taxonomy has at least one fixture or injection covering it, listed in a matrix test that fails when a kind is uncovered.
Ignoring SIGINT exits on SIGTERM in under 3 s local wall clock; ignoring both exits by SIGKILL with the process group reaped.
Pagination test returns all tools across three pages and respects the 500 cap by returning a clear cap-reached marker.
A 1 MiB stderr burst does not stall the handshake and the ring buffer holds the last 8 KiB.
After every test the fixture directory contains no orphan pid (checked by scanning child pids of the test process).
notes: Timing assertions use generous upper bounds to stay stable on CI; the ordering of signals is asserted, not their microsecond precision.

title: OAuth flow tests against a local authorisation server
description: Local hyper-based fake authorisation server and fake MCP HTTP server implementing RFC 8414 metadata, RFC 9728 protected resource metadata, RFC 7591 registration and PKCE code exchange, with knobs for wrong state, wrong verifier, expired token, 401 then success after refresh, and revoked refresh token. Tests drive the sign-in API without a browser by injecting a mock opener that performs the redirect to the loopback listener. Assert token storage in the keychain stub, refresh skew behaviour, single retry, removal of tokens from disk, and listener shutdown on cancel.
acceptance: Happy path completes, stores a token under oauth:<server>:<issuer> in the stub, and lists tools afterwards.
Expired access token triggers exactly one refresh and one retry; the server receives two calls, not a loop.
Revoked refresh token returns SignInRequired and clears the stored token row.
Wrong state and wrong verifier each fail with OAuthStateMismatch and no token is stored.
Cancelling closes the loopback listener within 1 s and leaves no binding behind (rebind test).
notes: No real network access in tests; the fake AS binds 127.0.0.1 on an ephemeral port.

title: MCP list projection query: servers x agents x health
description: One read model behind the list screen and the CLI list: mcp_list_rows(scope, project) joining items, deployments, locks, native_items and the newest health_checks row per server (window function or correlated index lookup, not a per-row scan). Each row carries id, display_name, scope, transport subtitle (command basename or url host), locked_by, latest health, and one cell per agent with state Linked | Off | Locked | Shadowed | Native { path } | None | NotInstalled, plus the resolved config path per cell. Native-only servers are synthesised from native_items with native_only=true and no canonical id. Chip counts come from this same row set so they cannot disagree with the table. Row order is name ascending with native-only rows last, matching the design.
acceptance: The 9-server fixture (7 managed, 2 native-only) returns 9 rows and chip counts All 9, Not in AgenTuna 2, Failing 1 that equal the filtered row counts.
A server with 300 health rows still yields exactly one row and the query plan references the (item_id, checked_at) index.
Cursor absent produces NotInstalled cells distinct from None cells for installed agents with no deployment; both render differently in the test snapshot.
A locked Global server reports locked_by=Global and Locked cells for every agent, and is excluded from failing counts.
Synthetic 500-server x 4-agent fixture returns in under 50 ms on the dev machine with an in-memory database.
notes: Adopt and Resolve actions mutate state through the migration slice; this story only supplies native rows and their paths.
